title: Premières questions de Tim Burchett aux témoins

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Merci M. le président. Merci, M. Garcia. J'aimerais juste vous avoir dans ma législation pour faire ça sur the reporting and we'll get together on that. Peut-être pouvez-vous be my co sponsor on that. Ca serait vraiment bien. Merci pour ces très bonnes questions. M. Graves, encore une fois, j'aimerais savoir, comment savez-vous que ce n'étaient pas des appareils à nous ?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Certains des comportements que nous avons observés dans a working area, we would see these objects being at 0.0 Mach. That's zero air speed over certain pieces of the ground. So what that means just like a river, if you throw a bobber in, it's going to float downstream. These objects were staying completely stationary in category four hurricane winds. These same objects would then accelerate to supersonic speeds 1.11.2 Mach. And they would do so in very erratic and quick behaviors that I don't have an explanation for.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. Have you spoken to commercial and military pilots that have seen these off of our East Coast?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I have.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. M. Faber. I noticed that in the Tic TAC video... - It's tic. TAC like the candy, not TikTok, like the Chinese communist app.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: That's correct.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Yes, sir. I just want to make that because my daughter corrected me on that and called me a boomer and said, hey, boomer. And I said, no, baby, it's Tic TAC, kike the candy. You're going to have to just look it up. But now I would also like to say today is a day of many. First, it's a miracle that we're having this meeting, and it's also a miracle that my wife has put up with me for nine years. Today today is my anniversary. So I want to tell my wife happy anniversary and that I love her very much. As she likes to say, this, nine years have been the best two years of her life. Thank you. M. Fravor, what astonished you the most about the flight capabilities of these Tic TACs? Very briefly.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: The performance, absolute performance.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: You're not aware of any other objects that anybody in the world has in this world that has those capabilities?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No, I think it's far beyond, actually, our material science that we currently possess. Are you aware of any other reconnaissance platforms that tracked or recorded the Tic TACs maneuvers? Maybe the NORAD system or any of the others? I am not.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. M. Grusch, thank you for being here, brother. Thank you all very much. Have you faced any retaliation or reprisals for any of your testimony or anything on these lines?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yeah, I have to be careful what I say in detail, because there is an open whistleblower reprisal investigation on my behalf, and I don't want to compromise that investigation by providing anything that may help provide somebody information. But it was very brutal and very unfortunate. Some of the tactics they used to hurt me, both professionally and personally, to be quite frank.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: It's very unfortunate. As they say, when you're over the target, that's when they do the most firing action. Do you have any personal knowledge of people who've been harmed or injured in efforts to cover up or conceal these extraterrestrial technology?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yes, personally.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Have anyone been murdered that you know of or have heard of?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I guess I have to be careful asking that question. I directed people with that knowledge to the appropriate authorities.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Maybe if we could get in a confidential area <abbr title="Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility">SCIF</abbr>, we could talk about that. But unfortunately, we were denied access to the <abbr title="Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility">SCIF</abbr>, and that's very unfortunate in this scenario.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: M. Faber, do you believe that you witnessed an additional object under the water in relation to your encounter?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I will say we did not see an object. There was something there to cause the whitewater, and when we turned around, it was gone. So there was something there that obviously moved.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. It was not the same object, though, that you were looking at, correct?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No, we actually joked that the Tic TAC was communicating with something when we came back, because the whitewater disappeared. We were, in another instance, were told about the capabilities of a jamming during viewing of some of when there were some people chasing some of these objects.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Did you experience any of that jamming or interrupting your radar or weapon system?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: My crew that launched after we landed experienced significant jamming to the APG 73 radar, which was what we had on board, which is a mechanically scanned, very high end system prior to the APG 79. And yes, it did pretty much everything you could do, range, velocity, aspect. And then it spit the lock, and the targeting pod is passive. That's what we were able to get the video on.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: I'm about to run out of time, but are you aware of any of our enemies that have that capability?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. I would also like to note for the record that, like George Knapp breaking Area 51, he's the reason I knew about that. And the reason I know about the Tic TACs is Leslie Keane from New York Times article. And I would encourage everybody to read that. Thank you, M. Chairman. Yield back to you for no time.
